text:
Maya Chen: Drafting a compact runloop for renewal signal mapping + consumption — want feedback before I turn this into the one‑pager. TL;DR: map signals -> risk tier -> enablement action -> telemetry to capture.
Alex Rivera: Love it. Can you paste the mapping table here? quick view helps.
Maya Chen: Sure — high level example: 
- Signal: sudden drop in weekly active requests -> Tier: High risk -> Action: Scheduled outreach + warmup pool bump
- Signal: token usage decline but same request count -> Tier: Medium -> Action: Prompting cadence review + onboarding checklist nudges
- Signal: increase in error rate (5xx) -> Tier: High -> Action: Ops escalation + temporary downgrade to lighter model variant
Jon Patel: For "warmup pool bump" we should add a recommended prefill pattern: staggered prefix prefill 3x over 30m to avoid surge.
Lisa Nguyen: Also capture whether they use streaming vs non‑streaming. Streaming clients tend to hit latency issues differently — add a telemetry flag: "streaming=true" so we can separate signals.
Maya Chen: Good call. I'm adding a small ops runbook snippet for prefill + batch sizing. Thoughts?
Alex Rivera: Drop it. Keep it practical. Example prefill command we give customers: 
```bash
# prefill 10 tenants with staggered delay
for t in $(cat tenant_ids.txt); do
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill -d '{"tenant": "$t", "tokens": 300}' &
  sleep 6
done
```
Jon Patel: Add note: prefer prefix caching for chat flows vs embedding caches for search. Prefix caching reduces KV lookups.
Maya Chen: OK adding that. Also including a short batching guidance: 
- Target batch latency window: 25–50ms for interactive routes; 150–400ms for bulk async.
- Max batch size depends on model and quantization; recommend starting at 8 and tune up.
Lisa Nguyen: Add a fallback policy snippet: if latency > SLO for 2 consecutive windows -> route to fallback model (cheaper or smaller) + flag customer for followup.
Maya Chen: Will do. Putting a simple decision tree: 
1) Detect signal -> 2) classify risk -> 3) apply quick mitigations (prefill, smaller model, rate cap) -> 4) schedule enablement touchpoint -> 5) collect feedback text + telemetry
CS Bot: Reminder: link to existing docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/prefill-guides and /ops/fallback-policies
Alex Rivera: For renewal risk scoring, can we capture time‑to-first‑decline? e.g., days since onboarding where key metrics fell below threshold. That's a strong leading indicator.
Maya Chen: Yes — adding features: time_to_drift, error_burst_count, streaming_fraction, avg_latency_percentile(95). Each should be a numeric feature stored in the cadence dashboard.
Jon Patel: Can we include a disposable checklist for customer enablement calls? short bullets.
Maya Chen: Draft checklist: 
- Confirm streaming vs non‑streaming usage
- Check recent prefill / batch config and last run time
- Validate error graphs (5xx, timeouts) + recent deploys
- Run a quick sample interaction and compare tokens vs expectation
- Agree on next 72h mitigation steps and owner
Lisa Nguyen: Add: capture customer's sentiment in a quick note (one phrase) and whether they accepted the mitigation plan. we use that in renewal scoring.
Alex Rivera: Love the sentiment capture. Could be values: "green/yellow/red".
Maya Chen: I'll add that. Also including a tiny snippet customers can paste to enable a lightweight streaming health export to our webhooks: 
```json
{"streaming_health_webhook": "https://hooks.redwood.ai/cs-streams/ingest", "interval": 300}
```
Jon Patel: Make sure we note security: only accept webhook from the tenant IP or signed header.
Maya Chen: noted. Security note added.
CS Bot: Incident link: recent surge runbook (INC-2025-44) referenced in the doc.
Lisa Nguyen: One more operational suggestion: during onboarding, set a 7‑day warm window with daily mini‑syncs for the first 72h if signal drift appears.
Maya Chen: Great — I'll make that the default in the runloop. Anyone want to volunteer to review the final one‑pager tomorrow?
Alex Rivera: I can do a pass in the morning.
Jon Patel: I can review the tactics section.
Lisa Nguyen: I'll review the enablement checklist and messaging.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. I'll update and post the one‑pager in #playbooks later today. :thumbsup:
CS Bot: Saved to /internal-cs/runloops/1763141592-renewal-mapping.md
Maya Chen: (for handoff) next steps: finalize doc, add sample metrics SQL, and attach to customer record templates. I'll ping when done.
